title: India Play Tajikistan Tonight in Dushanbe. The World Cup Starts in Six Days. Khalid Jamil Has a Depleted Squad and a Point to Prove.
excerpt: After a 1-0 loss to Zimbabwe and a disappointing Unity Cup, the Blue Tigers face a Tajikistan side with a new head coach, home advantage, and a winning record against India. Several Mohun Bagan players are missing. The June window has not started well.
body:
When India take the field in Dushanbe on Thursday evening, the FIFA World Cup will be six days away. India will not be at it. They have never been at one. But the timing of this friendly — sandwiched between a poor Unity Cup campaign and the start of the biggest football tournament on earth — makes it feel like more than a warm-up match.

Head coach Khalid Jamil's problems start with the squad list. Several Mohun Bagan Super Giant players were unavailable for the June international window, forcing India to travel with a modified 22-player group. Ryan Williams, who picked up a hamstring injury during the Unity Cup match against Jamaica, has been replaced by Parthib Sundar Gogoi. New faces include Mohammed Sanan Kundoyi, Vikram Partap Singh, and Macarton Louis Nickson — names that speak to opportunity, but also to the depth of India's absentee list.

## The Unity Cup Hangover

India's recent form offers little comfort. A 1-0 friendly defeat to Zimbabwe on May 30 extended a run of results that have tested patience. The Unity Cup campaign was disappointing by any measure, and Jamil has faced growing scrutiny over selection decisions and tactical approach.

The club-versus-country tensions that have plagued Indian football for years are once again front and centre. When the ISL runs through the international window and clubs resist releasing players, the national team inevitably fields a weaker side. It is a structural problem, not just a Jamil problem. But it is Jamil who must answer for the results.

## Tajikistan Under Angelovski

Tajikistan, by contrast, enter this match in a stable position. They have appointed Igor Angelovski — the Macedonian who led North Macedonia to their first European Championship in 2020 — as head coach, and this match marks his official debut on the touchline. For a Central Asian federation investing in long-term development, it is a statement hire.

Tajikistan have remained unbeaten since their last meeting with India and finished top of Group A in AFC Asian Cup qualifying. Playing at home in Dushanbe, they will use their physical advantage and altitude to control proceedings. The head-to-head record is sobering: six matches played, three Tajikistan wins, two India wins, one draw.

## What Jamil Needs

A win in Dushanbe would not solve India's structural problems, but it would buy Jamil breathing room. The squad he has assembled — built around Gurpreet Singh Sandhu in goal, Sandesh Jhingan and Rahul Bheke in defence, and Lallianzuala Chhangte providing attacking thrust — has enough quality to compete. Whether they can execute against a well-organised home side is another question.

The predicted 3-5-2 formation suggests Jamil wants to pack the midfield and play on the counter. Ricky Shabong and Macarton Louis Nickson offer energy in central areas, while Nikhil Poojary provides width. Up front, Vikram Partap and Farukh Choudhary carry the goal-scoring burden.

## The NRI Perspective

For Indian football fans in the diaspora, this match arrives at a bittersweet moment. The World Cup begins on June 11 in the United States, Canada, and Mexico — countries where millions of NRIs live. Four players of Indian origin — Sarpreet Singh for New Zealand, Tahsin Mohammed for Qatar, Nishan Velupillay for Australia, and Samuel Moutoussamy for DR Congo — will represent other nations at the tournament. India's own team will be playing friendlies in Central Asia.

The gap between where Indian football is and where it needs to be remains enormous. Matches like this one — away friendlies against mid-ranked Asian sides, with depleted squads, during windows that overlap with domestic leagues — are where the daily work of closing that gap happens. It is unglamorous, often invisible to casual fans, and frequently frustrating.

But it is also where the next generation of Indian footballers earns its minutes. Gogoi, Kundoyi, Nickson — if they perform in Dushanbe, they enter the conversation for the Asian Games later this year. If they do not, the cycle continues.

India's broadcast situation remains uncertain, with no confirmed television coverage for this match. Kick-off is scheduled for 8:30 PM IST from Dushanbe.
